reasons: Section 7.2 imposes the MFN/match obligation on Customer (our party) with no product scope, term limit, or comparison carve-outs — this is the rule's walk-away position and fails the fallback, so 'deviation' is correctly classified.

Redline guidance is followed exactly: the offending obligation in p0026 is deleted and no Vendor-granted MFN exists to preserve, so full deletion is the minimum edit that reaches the preferred position.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required tone and prefix, correctly notes the internal contradiction with Section 12.3's no-most-favoured-customer acknowledgment; no fallback offer is needed since the rule's preferred position is no MFN on Customer.
Deterministic check passes and the high change ratio is inherent to a deletion-type remedy expressly contemplated by the rule.
